about: webcpp::hash's capability table (spec section 3.5): which library implements each public name, over which hmacs, on which targets, and what upstream states about constant time. backend_has_v is the same table for the key derivations: test/capabilities_test.cpp compares them cell by cell, checks each type row against the code and each refusal text against its row; test/overrides_list_test.cpp checks detail/overrides.hpp against the overridable algorithms. The documentation renders from it.

layout.schema: This description. The version of the layout is "version"; a change of layout raises it.
layout.backends[]: Each library a function runs on: name (as cells name it), tag (its webcpp::hash::backends type, or null for a library without one in this increment: xkcp, blake3), macro (the word of WEBCPP_HASH_HAS_<macro>, WEBCPP_HASH_PROFILE_BACKEND_<macro> and WEBCPP_HASH_DEFAULT_BACKEND_<ALGORITHM>_<macro>), library (name and pin), licence, jamfile (the target a program names), targets (where it builds), portable (whether the portable profile may choose it: present on every target).
layout.hmacs: The hmac columns of a function over an hmac: the aliases of <webcpp/hash/hmac.hpp>, and "other", hmac<H> over any other Boost.Hash2 hash whose result is a digest.
layout.algorithms[]: One row group of spec 3.5: name, macro (the <ALGORITHM> of an override), tag (its kdfs:: type, or null), chapter (the documentation's chapter: digests, macs, kdfs, password_hashing, non-cryptographic), standard, overridable (whether default_backend chooses its backend, so that it has the overrides of detail/overrides.hpp), functions.
layout.functions[]: One public name: name, kind ("type": a Boost.Hash2-form type; "function": a function template with a Backend parameter), tag (the kdfs:: type of backend_has_v and default_backend, for a function), header, backends.
layout.backends{}: Per backend name, the cell: since (the increment it came with), hmacs (the columns it has, or null for a function or type that takes no hmac), constant_time {value: "yes", "no" or "not stated", source: where upstream says so, or what was read and says nothing}. A cell holds on every target of its backend.
